Headteacher's WELCOME
We are a vibrant and inclusive school community with over 1100 students on roll. Our school has an established history of excellent practice, strong pastoral care and high expectations. We aim to work closely with our different stakeholders to ensure that each and every student who comes through our door gets the very best opportunities that will set them on the path for an exciting, successful and fulfilling future.
Enjoy the website. If you require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Students' WELCOME
At Springfield, we have an enriched academic culture, as well as extracurricular activities and opportunities outside of school. Students are encouraged to work hard in a wide range of subjects and discover their own passions and interests through programmes such as the Brilliant Club, The Council of Portsmouth Students and the Girls' Network. The school also offers brilliant sport clubs using our amazing facilities including the tennis courts, fitness suite and sports halls. Overall, Springfield has a very supportive community and engaging teachers willing to offer their time and effort to help students.
UPCOMING EVENTS
SPRINGFIELD NEWS
TESTIMONIALS
"I find it incredibly rewarding to work in a space that prioritises both innovative learning and the continuous professional development of its staff."
"Although I'm in my first year, it has been an amazing experience so far. The staff are very kind and are willing to help if you are struggling. At Springfield there are many different opportunities to take part in, including trips and after school clubs which are open to all year groups and a great way to make new friends."
"It is a privilege to work with the amazing students at Springfield School. Everyday is different, and it's a joy to be part of their learning journey."
"Our school is very supportive and all the teachers are very kind. Another good thing is that there are a lot of after school clubs every day which we can join, boosting our confidence and learning something new."
"What I love most about Springfield is the way it celebrates hard work and achievement. Students feel genuinely recognised and encouraged, not just corrected. It creates a really positive atmosphere to work and learn in."
"It is a pleasure to be in this school and to work with all the wonderful teachers and students. I am excited to carry on my journey at Springfield!"

Careers Curriculum Statement
At Springfield School, we empower pupils to navigate diverse academic and vocational pathways through impartial advice and aspirational opportunities. Our Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) programme is a progressive, Year 7–11 journey designed to broaden horizons and foster independent, global citizenship.
Aligned with the Gatsby Benchmarks, our provision ensures every student benefits from:
Curriculum Integration - Linking classroom learning to the labour market.
Employer Encounters - Annual visits from professionals and apprenticeship providers.
Higher Education - Strong partnerships with the Universities of Portsmouth, Oxford, and Southampton.
Practical Experience - Year 10 work experience and 1:1 specialist guidance in Year 11.
Delivered through our PDL programme, assemblies, and workshops, we regularly review our impact via student and parent feedback. We welcome support from our community - if you can assist with talks or mock interviews, please contact Ms Burden via contact@springfield.uk.net.
As we prepare for our next policy review in February 2027, we remain guided by one core principle: The future depends on what you do today.

PE Clubs Fayre
During their lunch break on Friday, 03 September 2026, Year 7 and 8 students visited the Sports Hall to engage with our first ever PE Clubs Fayre. The fayre was a great opportunity for them to example some of the fun and engaging sporting activities that take place after school. Students competed in rowing, shooting and table tennis challenges with the winners receiving prizes. They learned of the varied sporting clubs that are available for them to join and had the chance to sign up. Extra curricular sports clubs are free to attend and are especially important for students wanting to, or who are already taking Sports Studies and GCSE PE. Taking part in sports clubs helps students improve not only their physical health but also their mental health and the chance to make new friends and gain new skills.
It has been exciting to see so many students sign up and take part in the clubs already. To join a club students can speak with their Tutor or a member of the PE team.

Mountbatten Centre Careers Experience
As part of our commitment to giving students workplace experience, five Year 9 students attended a careers-focused trip to the Mountbatten Centre on 23 April. The group toured the centre and learned about different roles in the fitness industry, including operations, front of house, lifeguard and fitness instructor. Year 9 students were able to try out different pieces of equipment in the gym, after being inducted, and finished by designing their own fitness routine for a client, as a personal trainer would have to do.
This trip gave students valuable insights into the fitness industry while enhancing their practical knowledge and motivation. These experiences not only enrich their education but also prepare them for future career opportunities.
We are grateful to the Solent Careers Hub and the Mountbatten Centre for offering the group such an interesting and enjoyable opportunity. Thanks also to Miss Matthews for accompanying the trip.

Personal Development
Springfield’s Personal Development programme is designed to equip students with the character, resilience, and knowledge they need to thrive in modern society. We provide a comprehensive curriculum that integrates PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic education) and RSHE (Relationships, Sex and Health Education), offering students a safe, age-appropriate space to explore their wellbeing, rights, and responsibilities. Alongside this, our robust Careers Education programme raises aspirations from Year 7 onwards, connecting classroom learning to future pathways through expert guidance and employer encounters.
Careers
Our vision of careers education is for every student to find the right next step and to have developed the skills and sense of responsibility needed to forge a career in an increasingly globalised, technological and evolving world. Policy and practice are guided by the principle that: The future depends on what you do today. Careers Education at Springfield has been accredited as an Area of Excellence by Challenge Partners.
Our Careers Guidance contacts are:
Mrs Laura Burden
Laura Burden is qualified to Level 7 in school careers leading. You can contact Laura on 02392 379119 or by email: contact@springfield.uk.net
Mrs Tracy Bailey
Tracy will be in school on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Contact Tracy by email: careers.adviser@springfield.uk.net
Tracy can help students with information, advice and guidance (IAG) on:
Post 16 options - college, Sixth Form, apprenticeship, work with
training and traineeships.
Higher Education and post 18 options.
Putting together a C.V., interview tips and job search.
Finding out what career or job you would like to do.
Labour market information.
Website: www.ebpsouth.co.uk
Mrs Rebecca Millar
You can contact Mrs Millar on 02392 379119 or by email: contact@springfield.uk.net
Work experience
Our work experience runs every July for all Year 10 students. Work experience bridges the gap between the classroom and the world of work, helping Year 10 students build essential employability skills and make informed decisions about their post-16 pathways. The school's work experience programme runs every July for students in Year 10; students are encouraged to develop their skills of communication, time management, problem solving, teamwork and professionalism.

Alumni
Simply put, an Alumnus (plural: Alumni) is a former student of a school. Even though our students move on after Year 11, they remain part of the school's history and legacy; some even visit us again to share their career journey as a guest speaker or mentor. We are always interested to learn of the experiences of our Alumni, whether they left last year or decades ago, so please do get in touch via contact@springfield.uk.net

Academic Results
We were delighted to congratulate our Year 11 students on their fantastic achievements in 2025/26. Students' efforts, supported by our staff and their families, led to positive academic progress across a variety of subjects.
The school’s provisional results indicate some excellent individual achievements and a sound performance by the cohort as a whole:
● Over 70% of students secured a grade 4 or higher in GCSE English, and 70% of students secured a grade 4 or higher in GCSE Mathematics; a sound 62% of students achieved a grade 4 or higher in both.
● High-Achieving Results – a total of 320 grades achieved by our students were at the higher level of grades 7 to 9; and well over two thirds of all grades were grade 4 or higher.
● Excellent results were achieved in several departments, including Music with a 100% pass rate at grade 4 or above, Biology at 99% grade 4 or above, and German at 94% grade 4 or above.
● An impressive 79% of the students taking Further Mathematics secured a grade 5 or higher in this advanced option.
● The school’s overall Attainment 8 score has risen by 1.7 points since last year, indicating steady school-wide improvement across the curriculum.
● GCSE Statistics - 100% of Year 10 students achieved a grade 4 or above.

SEND
Springfield is an inclusive school that recognises the needs of all individuals and endeavours to make pupils as independent as possible, whilst preparing them for adult life post 16.
All students are valued and encouraged to achieve to the best of their ability. Learning Support at Springfield strives to support all those who need it, which includes:
Students with an Education Health Care Plan.
Students with special educational needs who do not have an EHCP but who need support in some of their lessons, especially with their literacy.
Students with special educational needs who do not have an EHCP but who need support with social, emotional and mental health needs which can act as a barrier to learning.
Students with disabilities that impact on their ability to access the curriculum.
The SENDCO coordinates Learning Support via close liaison with Year Teams and Heads of Department. This is done on an individual basis, where the targeted support is provided on a needs-led basis.
Provision to meet the variety of special needs in the school is made through:
Adapted approaches by the class teacher of tasks and outcomes within the classroom.
In-class support provided by the Learning Support Team.
Individual and small group withdrawal of some students for intensive literacy support.
ELSA providing emotional literacy support to those who require it.
Small group work with students who have social, emotional and mental health difficulties which impacts on their readiness for some mainstream lessons
SEND and alternative provision at Springfield is responsive to the presenting needs of our students and is under constant internal review to ensure our offer remains appropriate.
Prospective students and their parents/carers are welcome to contact the SENCO (Lian Miveld) to arrange a visit to discuss any aspect of access arrangements.
